capabilities: Expose vault notes and metadata to AI clients via an MCP server
Search notes by text, regex, tags, and frontmatter filters
Create, update, patch, rename, and batch-write notes atomically
Run Dataview DQL queries through the Dataview plugin API
disambiguation: Not a general vault-maintenance toolkit; its job is exposing the vault to AI clients via an MCP server.
extras: Desktop-only; binds to 127.0.0.1 with a per-vault bearer token. Supports multiple vaults via configurable ports and installation via BRAT. Not manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
problem: Obsidian offers no built-in way for local AI clients to access and modify vault notes through a standard protocol.

relations.evidence: execute Dataview DQL through the enabled Dataview plugin API and return JSON-safe structured data

summary: MCP server plugin that lets local AI clients read, search, create, and update vault notes, metadata, and frontmatter over localhost.
